detailed_description: The Coin Flipper is a simple browser-side coin toss tool. Set a flip count between 1 and 100, click Flip, and the tool runs a short spin animation, then uses Math.random with a 50/50 split to produce that many heads or tails results. The latest result is shown as a large coin face and label, with a running history of up to 100 flips, heads/tails counts and percentages, a percentage bar, and the most recent 50 flips as small chips. Clear resets the current result and history. It does not use cryptographic randomness, weighted bias, 3D physics, seeds, sessions, localStorage persistence, or CSV export.
usage_steps: Set the flip count between 1 and 100
Click Flip to run a short spin animation and generate that many heads or tails outcomes
Read the latest result shown as the large coin face with the heads or tails label
Review the statistics card with heads count, tails count, total flips, and percentages
Scan the recent flips strip showing the latest 50 results as H or T chips
Click Clear to reset the current result and the stored history
usage_examples: Make a quick yes-or-no decision by flipping a single coin in the browser
Run a small batch of up to 100 flips and read how the heads and tails percentages compare
Show a child how repeated coin tosses approach an even split using the percentage bar
Pick who goes first in a casual game by sharing the on-screen result
